problems: The new RELA, CASZ1 and HMGA1 lookup results (E25-E27) are not-tested results for Hep 3B2.1-7; they do not count as evidence against occupancy and do not strengthen the binding predictions.
All binding claims rest on in-vitro models. No cellular occupancy or perturbation evidence is provided for these candidates.
No regulatory element is established at the variant: E03 and E05 report no overlapping cCRE, and no cited evidence links the site to FAM110B.
FAM110B remains a weak target candidate based on distance and keyword hits; no variant-to-gene link is shown, and E09 reports no significant GTEx eQTL.
No cited evidence establishes a connection between any chain and LDL cholesterol.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping RELA peak in the stated cell line would provide direct occupancy evidence and strengthen H1 relative to the binding-only alternatives.
A variant-overlapping CASZ1 peak would materially change the assessment of H2, especially given its reported low expression.
A variant-overlapping HMGA1 peak could make H3 more competitive despite the disagreement between its in-vitro model directions.

critique.next_experiment: In Hep 3B2.1-7 cells, perform an endogenous G-to-T base edit with matched controls, measure expression of nearby candidate genes (including FAM110B and CYP7A1), and assay allele-dependent TF occupancy at the edited site. This would test both regulatory activity and the proposed target-gene link.
